Meshwire

An independent MCP server for Blender. Control Blender from any MCP client, with tools for modeling, materials, sculpting, animation, AI 3D generation, and Microsoft Flight Simulator content.

Quick start · Tools · Self-refinement loop · Security · Documentation

Status: every pull request runs each tool in real Blender 4.5 LTS and 5.2 LTS. 190 of 225 tools work on both. 35 need what a headless test cannot provide, such as a GUI, network access, or an earlier call. Each list is under Tools, and fixes are tracked in the issues.

What is Meshwire?

Meshwire is an MCP server for AI clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex CLI. The server speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio. A Blender addon listens on a local TCP socket and runs each command on Blender's main thread through bpy.app.timers.

┌─────────────────┐    stdio     ┌─────────────────┐   TCP/JSON-RPC   ┌─────────────────┐
│  MCP client     │ ◄──────────► │   MCP Server    │ ◄──────────────► │  Blender Addon  │
│  (Claude / …)   │              │  (Python proc)  │  9876 to 9885    │  (bpy.app.timers)│
└─────────────────┘              └─────────────────┘                  └─────────────────┘
  • Blender coverage: scene, object, mesh, material, modifier, animation, render, export, baking, geometry nodes, sculpting, rigging, physics, and annotations.
  • MSFS content: LOD, collision, material, animation, and livery tools for Microsoft Flight Simulator. These tools now run in the test harness, but no generated package has been loaded in the sim yet, so treat their output as unproven until it has.
  • AI 3D generation: text and image to 3D through Hyper3D Rodin, Meshy, Tripo, TripoSR, Stable Fast 3D, Hunyuan3D, and ComfyUI.
  • Self-refinement loop: render an object from several angles, score it with an Ollama vision model, and iterate.
  • Poly Haven: free HDRIs, textures, and models with no API key.

Quick start

1. Run the MCP server

Meshwire is in alpha, so ask for pre-releases. With uv there is nothing to install up front:

uvx --prerelease allow meshwire --help

Or with pip:

pip install --pre meshwire

2. Install the Blender addon

Download blender_mcp_addon-<version>.zip from Releases, or build it from source:

git clone https://github.com/RFingAdam/meshwire
cd meshwire
python scripts/package_addon.py
# creates dist/blender_mcp_addon-<version>.zip

In Blender, open Edit > Preferences > Add-ons, choose Install from Disk from the menu at the top right, select the ZIP, and enable Meshwire. Host, port and API keys are add-on preferences, stored per user, so a shared .blend file carries none of them.

execute_script is off until you turn it on. Open the Meshwire tab in the 3D Viewport sidebar and click Allow Python. It stays on until Blender closes and is off again at every start.

3. Configure your MCP client

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "blender": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--prerelease", "allow", "meshwire"]
    }
  }
}

If you installed with pip, use "command": "meshwire" with no args.

4. Connect

  1. In Blender's 3D viewport, press N and open the Meshwire tab.
  2. Click Start Server.
  3. Restart your MCP client. The Blender tools appear in its tool list.

Then try:

Create a red cube at (2, 0, 0), add a subdivision surface modifier with 2 levels, and render it to /tmp/render.png.

Tools

Each tool is run in headless Blender with valid input, with every value of each enum, and with no arguments at all. A tool counts as working when every valid call succeeds or returns the error it should. That does not prove the output is right, so a second test drives Blender through the real socket and checks the result for core tools such as object creation, render, and bake. Self-refinement loop

The agent writes mesh code, renders from several angles, an Ollama vision model scores the result, and the agent applies fixes until the score stops improving.

┌───────────┐  execute_script  ┌─────────┐  render_multi_angle  ┌──────────────┐
│  agent    │ ──────────────► │ Blender  │ ───────────────────► │  PNG images  │
│  (LLM)    │                 │  (bpy)   │                      └──────┬───────┘
└─────┬─────┘                 └─────────┘                              │
      │                                                  analyze_viewport
      │  apply fix                                                     │
      │  (loop)                                                        ▼
      │                                                     ┌──────────────────┐
      └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────│  Ollama Vision   │
                              feedback + score              │ llama3.2-vision  │
                                                            └──────────────────┘

# 1. Open a refinement session
blender_refine_create_session(object_name="Tree", prompt="A realistic low-poly pine tree")

# 2. Generate an initial mesh
blender_execute_script(script="import bmesh; ...")

# 3. Evaluate
blender_refine_iteration(object_name="Tree", iteration=0, max_iterations=5)

# 4. Apply fixes from the feedback, then evaluate again
blender_execute_script(script="# fix issues from analysis ...")
blender_refine_iteration(object_name="Tree", iteration=1, previous_score=0.6)

# 5. Inspect the session
blender_refine_get_session(session_id="...")

See docs/usage.md for a walkthrough.

External integrations

Poly Haven

Poly Haven provides free HDRIs, textures, and 3D models with no API key. Downloads are cached locally.

blender_polyhaven_search(query="brick", asset_type="textures")
blender_polyhaven_download(asset_id="brick_wall_001", resolution="2k")

Cloud setup:

export RODIN_API_KEY="your-rodin-key"
export MESHY_API_KEY="your-meshy-key"
export TRIPO_API_KEY="your-tripo-key"

Local setup:

# TripoSR is not on PyPI: clone it and put it on PYTHONPATH
git clone https://github.com/VAST-AI-Research/TripoSR
pip install -r TripoSR/requirements.txt
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/TripoSR:$PYTHONPATH"

ollama pull llama3.2-vision:11b   # vision model for evaluation and refinement

Usage:

blender_ai_generate_model(prompt="a wooden chair", style="realistic")
blender_ai_generate_model(image_path="/path/to/image.png")
blender_ai_model_status(job_id="abc123", auto_import=true)

Styles: realistic, cartoon, low_poly, sculpture, anime. Formats: glb (default), gltf, fbx, obj, usdz.

Security

The addon's socket has no authentication yet. blender_execute_script runs arbitrary Python inside Blender, so it is off by default: it refuses every call until you click Allow Python in the Meshwire sidebar tab. Only that button turns it on, and nothing a client sends or a .blend file holds can. It resets whenever Blender starts. While the socket has no authentication, any process on your machine that can reach the port can still use the other tools, and can run code as you once you allow Python.

  • Only start the server on a machine you trust, and stop it when you're done.
  • Keep the host set to localhost. Don't bind it to 0.0.0.0 or expose the add-on's ports (9876 to 9885).
  • Don't run untrusted prompts or scripts against a Blender session with work you care about.

Authentication is planned for the next stable release (#12).

blender_ai_configure_backend accepts only enabled, api_key, host (an http or https URL), timeout and device. Paths and endpoints (ComfyUI workflow, model paths, base URLs) are set in Preferences > Add-ons > Meshwire.

Configuration

meshwire [--host HOST] [--port PORT]

  --host HOST   Blender addon host (default: 127.0.0.1)
  --port PORT   Blender addon port (default: find it, see below)

Which Blender the server talks to is decided in this order:

  1. --port, if given.
  2. The MESHWIRE_PORT environment variable, if set.
  3. Discovery. Each running add-on publishes a small file in instances/ inside the Meshwire config folder (next to the token), and the server picks the most recently started Blender that answers. It looks again at every connection, so a Blender that starts or restarts later is found, and it logs the port, Blender version and .blend file it chose. Discovery runs only when --host is a loopback address.
  4. Port 9876.

An explicit port is never second-guessed by discovery. With several Blenders open and no port given, the newest one wins; pass --port to talk to another.

In Blender, the Meshwire tab sets the socket port and starts or stops the server. Port 0 (the default) takes the first free port from 9876 to 9885, so a second Blender simply gets the next one. A port you set yourself is bound exactly or the start fails with a message saying why.

Blender versions

Meshwire supports Blender 4.2 through 5.2. Blender 4.5 LTS and 5.2 LTS are tested on every pull request. Blender 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 5.0 and 5.1 are tested nightly on a best-effort basis.

Troubleshooting

"Connection refused": make sure Blender is running, the Meshwire tab shows the server running, and the port matches.

"Python execution is off": click Allow Python in the Meshwire sidebar tab. It resets whenever Blender starts.

"Tool not found": restart your MCP client after editing its config, confirm the server command runs on its own with --help, and check the client's MCP log.

Addon doesn't appear in Blender: check Blender's system console for errors and try reinstalling the ZIP.

Poly Haven downloads fail: check your connection, confirm the asset ID exists on polyhaven.com, and check disk space.

AI generation doesn't work: blender_ai_list_backends shows backend status. Check your API keys for cloud backends (Preferences > Add-ons > Meshwire, or the RODIN_API_KEY and MESHY_API_KEY environment variables), or your models and VRAM for local ones. Follow a job with blender_ai_model_status.

Development

git clone https://github.com/RFingAdam/meshwire
cd meshwire
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate   # .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows
pip install -e ".[dev]"

pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/blender_integration_test.py   # unit tests
python -m tests.harness.driver --help   # truth harness, needs Blender; see CONTRIBUTING.md
ruff check .
ruff format .
python scripts/package_addon.py   # builds the addon ZIP
